## Natural history notes

A small lady beetle characterized by a rounded, glossy body, dark coloration, and three reddish to orange spots or patches that give it the “thrice-struck” appearance. In Florida, the Thrice-struck Lady Beetle is likely found in warm wooded and semi-open habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, gardens, parks, shrubs, and trees where aphids and scale insects occur. Both adults and larvae are predators of small soft-bodied insects, especially aphids, scales, and related plant-feeding pests, making them beneficial members of garden and forest-edge food webs.
